migration.description: Add a one-shot PostgreSQL migration and replica-bootstrap contract for the derived analytics target while retaining SQLite as the business-fact authority.
migration.release_unit_description: Managed PostgreSQL analytics schema, role, readiness, cutover, and forward-repair design.

durable_state.description: PostgreSQL role/grant ownership, ordered schema-migration ledger, analytics replica facts, applied-change identities, checkpoints, source coverage acknowledgements, and eligibility fences. SQLite business facts and the source journal remain authoritative.
durable_state.storage_implementation: PostgreSQL cvm_analytics schema plus the existing SQLite analytics source journal; no business-write state moves to PostgreSQL.

source_compatibility_range.from_program_versions: Existing deployments using the ADR 0051 pre-provisioned PostgreSQL foundation and supported SQLite source-journal states.
source_compatibility_range.to_program_version: Current managed-migration release candidate; release identity is selected by repository publication policy.

ddl_structural_changes.description: Reconcile the fixed owner, reader, application, and maintenance role contract; establish cvm_analytics ownership and the schema-migration ledger without dropping or cascading over unexpected objects.

Apply ordered additive schema migrations and grants. Transactional DDL stays in one migration unit; PostgreSQL operations that cannot run in a transaction are isolated ledger steps with explicit retry/repair recognition.

dml_changes.description: Record the migration identity and checksum, fence service eligibility, and move a caught-up replica to bootstrapping before any semantic or replica-shape rebuild.

historical_data_backfill_or_transformati.description: Run the explicit bounded SQLite-source snapshot/bootstrap into derived PostgreSQL facts, keys, applied-change identities, checkpoints, and coverage acknowledgements. This is not a business-write migration or an automatic raw-data backfill.

progress_signals: Migration ledger identity, checksum, state, and minimum-reader compatibility.
Catalog ownership, role attributes, PUBLIC privileges, and exact grant probes.
Replica lifecycle, semantic version, baseline, source/target checkpoints, coverage revision, and bounded error code.
Separate core_ready and analytics_ready conditions, including a repeatable-read read-only probe.
pause_points: After target/role preflight and after each committed schema-ledger unit.
After the compatibility fence and before target cleanup.
Between bounded bootstrap batches and before source acknowledgement publishes eligibility.
Before process start and before traffic admission.

recovery.program_rollback_state_behavior: Rollback changes application selection back to SQLite; it does not reverse-copy business facts, drop PostgreSQL state, or down-migrate an applied ledger entry.
recovery.faulty_release_recovery: Repair forward with a recognized idempotent migration or a later compatible release. A stopped or failed bootstrap leaves the target fenced and unavailable until the source/target cause is understood and the bounded bootstrap is rerun.

required_test_evidence: Fresh disposable PostgreSQL 18 target proves role ownership, exact grants, ledger creation, schema compatibility, and read-only verification.
Repeated migration is idempotent and preserves the same ledger/checksum/grant contract without an additive-only target reset.
Known older schema and legacy fact-date states are fenced, upgraded in order, rebuilt from a stable SQLite source, and admitted only after matching checkpoints and projections.
Failures after each committed step, after the fence, and during a bounded bootstrap batch remain unavailable and repair forward to the same final state.

PostgreSQL outage, authentication/schema/permission mismatch, stale checkpoint, source gap, and schema-newer-than-reader all preserve SQLite facts and fail closed without fabricated analytics or implicit SQLite fallback.
Cutover waits for both core and analytics readiness; rollback restores SQLite selection without reverse-copy or target deletion.
